outcome: Mode of birth (labor induction or no-labor caesarean section)
cohort: The study included all women diagnosed with colorectal cancer during pregnancy or postpartum in New South Wales, Australia, with a comparison group of women who gave birth without cancer.
finding: The incidence of pregnancy-associated colorectal cancer significantly increased in New South Wales from 1994 to 2013, and women with gestational colorectal cancer experienced higher odds of severe maternal complications, planned preterm birth, and severe neonatal adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Women with gestational colorectal cancer had significantly higher odds of giving birth by labor induction or no-labor caesarean section.
